You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 36 to 45 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 36 至 45 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some performance evaluations require supervisors to take action. Employees who receive a very favorable evaluation may deserve some type of recognition or even a promotion. If supervisors do not acknowledge such outstanding performance, employees may either lose their 36 and reduce their effort or search for a new job at a firm that will 37 them for high performance. Supervisors should acknowledge high performance so that the employee will continue to perform well in the future.

Employees who receive unfavorable evaluations must also be given attention. Supervisors must 38 the reasons for poor performance. Some reasons, such as a family illness, may have a temporary adverse 39 on performance and can be corrected. Other reasons, such as a bad attitude, may not be temporary. When supervisors give employees an unfavorable evaluation, they must decide whether to take any 40 actions. If the employees were unaware of their own deficiencies, the unfavorable evaluation can pinpoint（指出）the deficiencies that employees must correct. In this case, the supervisor may simply need to monitor the employees 41 and ensure that the deficiencies are corrected.

If the employees were already aware of their deficiencies before the evaluation period, however, they may be unable or unwilling to correct them. This situation is more serious, and the supervisor may need to take action. The action should be 42 with the firm’s guidelines and may include reassigning the employees to new jobs, 43 them temporarily, or firing them. A supervisor’s action toward a poorly performing worker can 44 the attitudes of other employees. If no 45 is imposed on an employee for poor performance, other employees may react by reducing their productivity as well.

Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

paragraphs.sourceText: The College Essay: Why Those 500 Words Drive Us Crazy
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学作文：为什么这 500 个字让我们发疯

paragraphs.sourceText: one of several hundred thousand high-school seniors who had a painful fall. The deadline for applying to his favorite college was Nov. 1, and by early October he had yet to fill out the application. More to the point, he had yet to settle on a subject for the personal essay accompanying the application. According to college folklore, a well-turned essay has the power to seduce (诱惑）an admissions committee. “He wanted to do one thing at a time,” Meg says, explaining her son’s delay. “But really, my son is a huge procrastinator (拖延者). The essay is the hardest thing to do, so he’s put it off the longest.” Friends and other veterans of the process have warned Meg that the back and forth between editing parent and writing student can be traumatic（痛苦的）.
paragraphs.translationZh: 数十万高中生中的一名经历了痛苦的跌倒。申请他最喜欢的大学的截止日期是 11 月 1 日，但到 10 月初他还没有填写申请表。更重要的是，他还没有确定申请随附的个人论文的主题。根据大学民间传说，一篇精心设计的论文有诱惑招生委员会的力量。“他一次只想做一件事，”梅格在解释儿子的拖延时说，“但实际上，我儿子是一个严重的拖延者。论文是最难做的事情，所以他推迟了最长的时间。”朋友和其他经历过这个过程的老手警告梅格，编辑家长和写作学生之间的来回可能会很糟糕。创伤性的。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Back in the good old days — say, two years ago, when the last of my children suffered the ordeal (折磨)—a high-school student applying to college could procrastinate all the way to New Year’s Day of their senior year, assuming they could withstand the parental pestering (烦扰). But things change fast in the nail-biting world of college admissions. The recent trend toward early decision and early action among selective colleges and universities has pushed the traditional deadline of January up to Nov. 1 or early December for many students.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 回到过去的美好时光——比如说，两年前，当我的最后一个孩子遭受折磨时——一个申请大学的高中生可以一直拖延到高年级的元旦，假设他们能承受父母的纠缠。但在令人紧张的大学招生世界里，事情变化得很快。最近，选择性学院和大学的早期决定和早期行动趋势已将许多学生的传统 1 月截止日期推迟到 11 月 1 日或 12 月初。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) If the time for heel-dragging has been shortened, the true source of the anxiety and panic remains what it has always been. And ifs not the application itself. A college application is a relatively straightforward questionnaire asking for the basics: name, address, family history, employment history. It would all be innocent enough — 20 minutes of busy work — except it comes attached to a personal essay.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 如果拖后腿的时间缩短了，焦虑和恐慌的真正根源仍然是原来的样子。如果不是应用程序本身。大学申请是一份相对简单的问卷，询问基本信息：姓名、地址、家族史、工作经历。这一切都足够天真了——20分钟的忙碌工作——只不过它附有一篇个人论文。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) “There are good reasons it causes such anxiety,” says Lisa Sohmer, director of college counseling at the Garden School in Jackson Heights, N.Y. “It’s not just the actual writing. By now everything else is already set. Your course load is set, your grades are set, your test scores are set. But the essay is something you can still control, and it’s open-ended. So the temptation is to write and rewrite and rewrite.” Or stall and stall and stall.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 纽约州杰克逊高地花园学校的大学咨询主任丽莎·索默（Lisa Sohmer）说：“它引起这种焦虑是有充分理由的。这不仅仅是实际的写作。到目前为止，其他一切都已经确定了。你的课程负担已经确定，你的成绩已经确定，你的考试分数也已经确定。但论文仍然是你可以控制的，而且它是开放式的。所以你很想写、重写、重写。”或者停顿、停顿、停顿。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The application essay, along with its mythical importance, is a recent invention. In the 1930s, when only one in 10 Americans had a degree from a four-year college, an admissions committee was content to ask for a sample of applicants’ school papers to assess their writing ability. By the 1950s, most schools required a brief personal statement of why the student had chosen to apply to one school over another.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 申请论文及其神话般的重要性是最近的发明。在 20 世纪 30 年代，只有十分之一的美国人拥有四年制大学学位，招生委员会满足于要求申请人提供学校论文样本来评估他们的写作能力。到了 20 世纪 50 年代，大多数学校都要求学生提供一份简短的个人陈述，说明为什么选择申请一所学校而不是另一所学校。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Today nearly 70 percent of graduating seniors go off to college, including two-year and four- year institutions. Even apart from the increased competition, the kids enter a process that has been utterly transformed from the one baby boomers knew. Nearly all application materials are submitted online, and the Common Application provides a one-size-fits form accepted by more than 400 schools, including the nation’s most selective.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 如今，近 70% 的应届毕业生进入大学，包括两年制和四年制院校。即使除了日益激烈的竞争之外，孩子们也进入了一个与婴儿潮一代所知道的完全不同的过程。几乎所有申请材料都是在线提交的，通用申请提供了一份被 400 多所学校接受的通用表格，其中包括全国最挑剔的学校。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Those schools usually require essays of their own, but the longest essay, 500 words maximum, is generally attached to the Common Application. Students choose one of six questions. Applicants are asked to describe an ethical dilemma they’ve faced and its impact on them, or discuss a public issue of special concern to them, or tell of a fictional character or creative work that has profoundly influenced them. Another question invites them to write about the importance (to them, again) of diversity — a word that has assumed magic power in American higher education. The most popular option: write on a topic of your choice.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 这些学校通常需要自己的论文，但最长的论文（最多 500 字）通常附在通用申请表中。学生选择六个问题之一。申请者被要求描述他们所面临的道德困境及其对他们的影响，或者讨论他们特别关心的公共问题，或者讲述一个对他们产生深远影响的虚构人物或创意作品。另一个问题邀请他们写下多样性（再次对他们来说）的重要性——这个词在美国高等教育中具有魔力。最受欢迎的选择：写下您选择的主题。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) “Boys in particular look at the other questions and say, ‘Oh, that’s too much work,’” says John Boshoven, a counselor
paragraphs.translationZh: H) “男孩们尤其会在看到其他问题时说，‘哦，这太麻烦了，’”辅导员约翰·博斯霍文 (John Boshoven) 说道

paragraphs.sourceText: in the Ann Arbor, Mich., public schools. “They think if they do a topic of their choice, ‘I’ll just go get that history paper I did last year on the Roman Empire and turn it into a first-person application essay!’ And they end up producing something utterly ridiculous.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 在密歇根州安娜堡市的公立学校。 “他们认为，如果他们选择一个主题，‘我会去拿去年写的关于罗马帝国的历史论文，然后把它变成一篇第一人称申请论文！’而他们最终会写出一些完全荒谬的东西。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Talking to admissions professionals like Boshoven, you realize that the list of “don’ts” in essay writing is much longer than the “dos.” “No book reports, no history papers, no character studies,” says Sohmer.
paragraphs.translationZh: I）与像博斯霍文这样的招生专业人士交谈，你会意识到论文写作中“不要做”的清单比“应该做”的清单要长得多。 “没有读书报告，没有历史论文，没有人物研究，”索默说。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) ‘‘It drives you crazy, how easily kids slip into cliches(老生常谈)says Boshoven.“They don’t realize how typical their experiences are. ‘I scored the winning goal in soccer against our arch- rival’ ‘My grandfather served in World War II, and I hope to be just like him someday.’ That may mean a lot to that particular kid. But in the world of the application essay, it’s nothing. You’ll lose the reader in the first paragraph.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J) “这会让你发疯，孩子们很容易陷入陈词滥调，Boshoven 说。“他们没有意识到自己的经历有多么典型。‘我在足球比赛中对阵我们的主要对手，打进了致胜一球’‘我的祖父在第二次世界大战中服役，我希望有一天能像他一样。’这对那个孩子来说可能意义重大。但在申请论文的世界里，这没什么。你会在第一段中失去读者。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) “The greatest strength you bring to this essay,” says the College Board’s how-to book, “is 17 years or so of familiarity with the topic: YOU. The form and style are very familiar, and best of all, you are the world-class expert on the subject of YOU ... It has been the subject of your close scrutiny every morning since you were tall enough to see into the bathroom mirror. The key word in the Common Application prompts is “you.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 美国大学理事会的指导手册中写道，“你为这篇文章带来的最大优势是对这个主题的熟悉程度：17年左右：你。形式和风格都非常熟悉，最重要的是，你是关于你这个主题的世界级专家……自从你长到可以照镜子的时候，它就一直是你每天早上仔细审视的主题。通用申请提示中的关键词是“你”。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) The college admission essay contains the grandest American themes — status anxiety, parental piety （孝顺） intellectual standards — and so it is only a matter of time before it becomes infected by the country’s culture of excessive concern with self-esteem. Even if the question is ostensibly （表面上) about something outside the self (describe a fictional character or solve a problem of geopolitics), the essay invariably returns to the favorite topic: what is its impact on YOU?
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 大学入学论文包含了美国最宏大的主题——地位焦虑、父母孝顺的智力标准——所以它迟早会被这个国家过度关注自尊的文化所感染。即使问题表面上是关于自我之外的事情（描述一个虚构人物或解决地缘政治问题），这篇文章总是回到最喜欢的话题：它对你有什么影响？

paragraphs.sourceText: M) “For all the anxiety the essay causes,” says Bill McClintick of Mercersburg Academy in Pennsylvania, “it’s a very small piece of the puzzle. I was in college admissions for 10 years. I saw kids and parents beat themselves up over this. And at the vast majority of places, it is simply not a big variable in the college’s decision-making process.”
paragraphs.translationZh: M）“尽管这篇文章引起了人们的焦虑，”宾夕法尼亚州默瑟斯堡学院的比尔·麦克林蒂克（Bill McClintick）说，“这只是拼图中的一小部分。我从事大学招生工作已有10年了。我看到孩子们和家长们为此自责。在绝大多数地方，这根本不是学院决策过程中的一个大变量。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Many admissions officers say they spend less than a couple of minutes on each application, including the essay. According to a recent survey of admissions officers, only one in four private colleges say the essay is of “considerable importance” in judging an application. Among public colleges and universities, the number drops to roughly one in 10. By contrast, 86 percent place “considerable importance” on an applicant’s grades, 70 percent on “strength of curriculum.”
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 许多招生人员表示，他们在每份申请上花费的时间不到几分钟，包括论文。根据最近对招生人员的一项调查，只有四分之一的私立大学表示这篇文章在判断申请时“相当重要”。在公立学院和大学中，这一数字下降到大约十分之一。相比之下，86% 的人“非常重视”申请者的成绩，70% 的人“非常重视”“课程强度”。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Still, at the most selective schools, where thousands of candidates may submit identically high grades and test scores, a marginal item like the essay may serve as a tie-breaker between two equally qualified candidates. The thought is certainly enough to keep the pot boiling under parents like Meg, the lawyer-mom, as she tries to help her son choose an essay topic. For a moment the other day, she thought she might have hit on a good one. “His father’s from France,” she says. “I said maybe you could write about that, as something that makes you different. You know: half French, half American. I said, “You could write about your identity issues.’ He said, ‘I don’t have any identity issues!’ And he’s right. He’s a well-adjusted, normal kid. But that doesn’t make for a good essay, does it?”
paragraphs.translationZh: O）尽管如此，在最挑剔的学校，成千上万的候选人可能会提交相同的高成绩和考试成绩，像论文这样的边缘项目可能会成为两个同等资格的候选人之间的决胜局。当律师妈妈梅格试图帮助儿子选择论文主题时，这个想法肯定足以让父母们沸腾。有一天，她有那么一刻觉得自己可能碰上了一个好主意。 “他的父亲来自法国，”她说。 “我说也许你可以把它写下来，作为让你与众不同的东西。你知道：一半是法国人，一半是美国人。我说，“你可以写你的身份问题。”他说，“我没有任何身份问题！”他是对的。他是一个适应良好的正常孩子。但这并不构成一篇好文章，不是吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Today many universities require their applicants to write an essay of up to five hundred words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 如今，许多大学要求申请者写一篇最多五百字的论文。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. One recent change in college admissions is that selective colleges and universities have moved the traditional deadline to earlier dates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 大学招生方面最近的一项变化是，部分学院和大学将传统的截止日期提前。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Applicants and their parents are said to believe that the personal essay can sway the admissions committee.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 据说申请人及其家长相信个人论文可以影响招生委员会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Applicants are usually better off if they can write an essay that distinguishes them from the rest.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 如果申请者能写出一篇让自己与其他人区别开来的文章，那么他们的处境通常会更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Not only is the competition getting more intense, the application process today is also totally different from what baby boomers knew.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 不仅竞争变得更加激烈，今天的申请流程也与婴儿潮一代所知道的完全不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. In writing about their own experiences many applicants slip into cliches, thus failing to engage the reader.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 在写下自己的经历时，许多申请人陷入了陈词滥调，从而无法吸引读者。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. According to a recent survey, most public colleges and universities consider an applicant’s grades highly important.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 根据最近的一项调查，大多数公立学院和大学认为申请人的成绩非常重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. Although the application essay causes lots of anxiety, it does not play so important a role in the college’s decision-making process.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 尽管申请论文引起很多焦虑，但它在大学的决策过程中并没有发挥如此重要的作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. The question you are supposed to write about may seem outside the self, but the theme of the essay should center around its impact on you.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54.你要写的问题可能看起来与自我无关，但文章的主题应该围绕它对你的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. In the old days, applicants only had to submit a sample of their school papers to show their writing ability.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 过去，申请者只需提交学校论文样本即可证明其写作能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Among the government’s most interesting reports is one that estimates what parents spend on their children. Not surprisingly, the costs are steep. For a middle-class, husband-and-wife family (average pretax income in 2009: $76,250), spending per child is about $12,000 a year. With inflation the family’s spending on a child will total $286,050 by age 17.
paragraphs.translationZh: 政府最有趣的报告之一是估算父母在孩子身上的花费。毫不奇怪，成本高昂。对于一个中产阶级夫妻家庭（2009年平均税前收入：76,250美元）来说，每个孩子的支出每年约为12,000美元。考虑到通货膨胀，到 17 岁时，家庭在孩子身上的支出将达到 286,050 美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: The dry statistics ought to inform the ongoing deficit debate, because a budget is not just a catalog of programs and taxes. It reflects a society’s priorities and values. Our society does not一despite rhetoric (说辞) to the contrary — put much value on raising children. Present budget policies tax parents heavily to support the elderly. Meanwhile, tax breaks for children are modest. If deficit reduction aggravates these biases, more Americans may choose not to have children or to have fewer children. Down that path lies economic decline.
paragraphs.translationZh: 枯燥的统计数据应该为正在进行的赤字辩论提供信息，因为预算不仅仅是计划和税收的目录。它反映了社会的优先事项和价值观。尽管有相反的说法，我们的社会并没有非常重视抚养孩子。目前的预算政策对父母征收沉重的税收来赡养老年人。与此同时，针对儿童的税收减免力度不大。如果赤字削减加剧了这些偏见，更多的美国人可能会选择不生孩子或少生孩子。沿着这条路就是经济衰退。

paragraphs.sourceText: Societies that cannot replace their populations discourage investment and innovation. They have stagnant（萧条的） or shrinking markets for goods and services. With older populations, they resist change. To stabilize its population — discounting immigration — women must have an average of two children. That’s a fertility rate of 2.0. Many countries with struggling economies are well below that.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无法取代人口的社会会阻碍投资和创新。他们的商品和服务市场停滞或萎缩。对于老年人口，他们抵制变革。为了稳定人口（不考虑移民），女性必须平均生育两个孩子。那是2.0的生育率。许多经济陷入困境的国家远低于这一水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: Though having a child is a deeply personal decision, it’s shaped by culture, religion, economics, and government policy. “No one has a good answer” as to why fertility varies among countries, says sociologist Andrew Cherlin of The Johns Hopkins University. Eroding religious belief in Europe may partly explain lowered birthrates. In Japan young women may be rebelling against their mothers’ isolated lives of child rearing. General optimism and pessimism count. Hopefulness fueled America’s baby boom. After the Soviet Union’s collapse, says Cherlin, “anxiety for the future” depressed birthrates in Russia and Eastern Europe.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管生孩子是一个非常个人的决定，但它受到文化、宗教、经济和政府政策的影响。约翰·霍普金斯大学的社会学家安德鲁·切尔林表示，对于生育率为何因国家而异的问题，“没有人能给出一个好的答案”。欧洲宗教信仰的削弱可能是出生率下降的部分原因。在日本，年轻女性可能正在反抗母亲孤立的抚养孩子的生活。普遍的乐观和悲观情绪都很重要。希望推动了美国的婴儿潮。切尔林说，苏联解体后，“对未来的焦虑”导致俄罗斯和东欧的出生率下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: In poor societies, people have children to improve their economic well-being by increasing the number of family workers and providing support for parents in their old age. In wealthy societies, the logic often reverses. Government now supports the elderly, diminishing the need for children. By some studies, the safety nets for retirees have reduced fertility rates by 0.5 children in the United States and almost 1.0 in Western Europe, reports economist Robert Stein in the journal National Affairs. Similarly, some couples don’t have children because they don’t want to sacrifice their own lifestyles to the time and expense of a family.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在贫穷的社会中，人们生孩子是为了通过增加家庭工人的数量和为年老的父母提供支持来改善他们的经济福祉。在富裕社会，逻辑常常相反。政府现在支持老年人，减少了对儿童的需求。经济学家罗伯特·斯坦在《国家事务》杂志上报道说，根据一些研究，退休人员的安全网使美国的生育率降低了 0.5 个，西欧的生育率降低了近 1.0 个。同样，一些夫妇没有孩子，因为他们不想为了家庭的时间和开支而牺牲自己的生活方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Young Americans already face a bleak labor market that cannot instill (注入) confidence about having children. Piling on higher taxes won’t help. “If higher taxes make it more expensive to raise children, says Nicholas Eberstadt of the American Enterprise Institute, “people will think twice about having another child.” That seems like common sense, despite the multiple influences on becoming parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国年轻人已经面临着惨淡的劳动力市场，无法灌输对生孩子的信心。增加税收无济于事。美国企业研究所的尼古拉斯·埃伯施塔特表示，“如果更高的税收导致抚养孩子的成本更高，那么人们就会三思而行再要一个孩子。”尽管对成为父母有多重影响，但这似乎是常识。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Space exploration has always been the province of dreamers: The human imagination readily soars where human ingenuity (创造力）struggles to follow, A Voyage to the Moon, often cited as the first science fiction story, was written by Cyrano de Bergerac in 1649. Cyrano was dead and buried for a good three centuries before the first manned rockets started to fly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 太空探索一直是梦想家的领域：在人类的创造力（创造力）难以追随的地方，人类的想象力很容易飙升，《月球航行》通常被认为是第一个科幻小说故事，由西拉诺·德·贝尔热拉克于 1649 年写成。在第一艘载人火箭开始飞行之前，西拉诺已经去世并被埋葬了整整三个世纪。

paragraphs.sourceText: In 1961, when President Kennedy declared that America would send a man to the moon by the decade’s end, those words, too, had a dreamlike quality. They resonated（共鸣）with optimism and ambition in much the same way as the most famous dream speech of all, delivered by Martin Luther King Jr. two years later. By the end of the decade, both visions had yielded concrete results and transformed American society. And yet in many ways the two dreams ended up at odds with each other. The fight for racial and economic equality is intensely pragmatic (讲求实用的）and immediate in its impact. The urge to explore space is just the opposite. It is figuratively and literally otherworldly in its aims.
paragraphs.translationZh: 1961 年，当肯尼迪总统宣布美国将在本世纪末将人类送上月球时，这句话也具有梦幻般的品质。他们与乐观和雄心产生共鸣，就像两年后马丁·路德·金发表的最著名的梦想演讲一样。到本世纪末，这两个愿景都产生了具体成果，并改变了美国社会。然而，在很多方面，这两个梦想最终彼此矛盾。争取种族和经济平等的斗争是非常务实的，而且其影响是立竿见影的。探索太空的冲动恰恰相反。它的目标无论从形象上还是字面意义上都是超凡脱俗的。

paragraphs.sourceText: When the dust settled, the space dreamers lost out. There was no grand follow-up to the Apollo missions. The technologically compromised space shuttle program has just come to an end, with no successor. The perpetual argument is that funds are tight, that we have more pressing problems here on Earth. Amid the current concerns about the federal deficit, reaching toward the stars seems a dispensable luxury — as if saving one-thousandth of a single year’s budget would solve our problems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当尘埃落定后，太空梦想家们输了。阿波罗任务没有重大后续行动。技术上受到损害的航天飞机计划刚刚结束，没有继任者。永恒的争论是资金紧张，地球上有更紧迫的问题。在当前对联邦赤字的担忧中，追求明星似乎是一种可有可无的奢侈——仿佛节省一年预算的千分之一就能解决我们的问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: But human ingenuity struggles on. NASA is developing a series of robotic probes that will get the most bang from a buck. They will serve as modem Magellans, mapping out the solar system for whatever explorers follow, whether man or machine. On the flip side, companies like Virgin Galactic are plotting a bottom-up assault on the space dream by making it a reality to the public. Private spaceflight could lie within reach of rich civilians in a few years. Another decade or two and it
paragraphs.translationZh: 但人类的聪明才智仍在继续挣扎。美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 正在开发一系列机器人探测器，这些探测器将发挥最大作用。他们将充当现代麦哲伦人，为任何探索者（无论是人类还是机器）绘制太阳系地图。另一方面，像维珍银河这样的公司正在密谋对太空梦想进行自下而上的攻击，将其变成现实。几年后，私人太空飞行将成为富裕平民触手可及的事情。再过一两年就可以了

paragraphs.sourceText: could go mainstream.
paragraphs.translationZh: 可以成为主流。

paragraphs.sourceText: The space dreamers end up benefiting all of us — not just because of the way they expand human knowledge, or because of the spin-off technologies they produce, but because the two types of dreams feed off each other. Both Martin Luther King and John Kennedy appealed to the idea that humans can transcend what were once considered inherent limitations. Today we face seeming challenges in energy, the environment, health care. Tomorrow we will transcend these as well, and the dreamers will deserve a lot of the credit. The more evidence we collect that our species is capable of greatness, the more we will actually achieve it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 太空梦想家最终使我们所有人受益——不仅因为他们扩展人类知识的方式，或者因为他们产生的衍生技术，还因为这两种类型的梦想相互促进。马丁·路德·金和约翰·肯尼迪都主张人类可以超越曾经被认为是固有的局限性。今天，我们在能源、环境、医疗保健方面面临着看似严峻的挑战。明天我们也将超越这些，梦想家将得到很多荣誉。我们收集的证据越多，表明我们的物种有能力实现伟大，我们就越能真正实现这一目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2. 中国人自古以来就在中秋时节庆祝丰收。这与北美地区庆祝感恩节的习俗十分相似。过中秋节的习俗于唐代早期在中国各地开始流行。中秋节在农历八月十五，是人们拜月的节日:这天夜晚皓月当空，人们合家团聚，共赏明月。2006 年，中秋节被列为中国的文化遗产，2008 年又被定为公共假日。月饼被视为中秋节不可或缺的美食。 人们将月饼作为礼物馈赠亲友或在家庭聚会上享用。传统的月饼上带有“麦（longevity) ”、“福”或“和”等字样。
